nodes.text: before king and commoner, may be killed and deserve death, wherever they are found.
On *óbótamál* [crimes that cannot be atoned for with a fine]. Chapter
And those who lose their lives on account of theft
or brigandage, whether they rob on ships or on land,
and likewise for murder and witchcraft, for soothsaying and *útisetur* [sitting out at night], to wake
up trolls, to practise heathenism by it; and likewise those men who become hired assassins
to kill men with whom they have no quarrel, and
take money for it, unless the king's officer has [them] punished to cleanse the land
